title: Angels, Satan and Demons
summary: What the Bible teaches about the unseen world: holy angels, the fall of Satan, demons, and the believer's victory in Christ.
description: Many people in Africa live with a strong awareness of the spirit world, and with fear. This course sets out what Scripture teaches about angels, Satan and demons, avoiding both unbelief and superstition. It shows Christ's complete victory over the powers of darkness and how believers stand firm in spiritual warfare, including the different views Christians hold about deliverance ministry.
objectives: Teach what Scripture says about the nature and work of angels
Explain the origin, character and limits of Satan and demons
Show Christ's victory over the powers of darkness
Equip believers to stand firm in spiritual warfare without fear
outcomes: Describe the creation, nature and ministry of angels
Explain Satan's names, tactics and certain defeat
Distinguish biblical teaching from folk beliefs about spirits
Explain the armour of God in Ephesians 6
Describe fairly the views on whether believers can be demonised

modules.title: The Holy Angels
modules.intro: Angels are real created spirits who serve God and His people. This week we study what they are and what they do.

lessons.title: Created spirits
lessons.body:
Angels are created beings: "by him were all things created... visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers" (Colossians 1:16). They are spirits (Hebrews 1:14), though they can appear in human form (Genesis 18:2; Hebrews 13:2).

They are powerful (Psalm 103:20) but not all-powerful, all-knowing or everywhere present. They are numerous: "ten thousand times ten thousand" (Revelation 5:11).

Scripture names two: **Michael**, the archangel (Jude 1:9), and **Gabriel**, who announced the births of John and Jesus (Luke 1:19, 26). It also mentions cherubim and seraphim (Genesis 3:24; Isaiah 6:2).

lessons.title: What angels do
lessons.body:
Angels **worship** God continually (Isaiah 6:3; Revelation 5:11-12). They are God's **messengers**; the word *angel* means messenger (Luke 1:26-28).

They **serve and protect** believers: "Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?" (Hebrews 1:14). "The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them" (Psalm 34:7). An angel freed Peter from prison (Acts 12:7).

They will accompany Christ at His return and gather His elect (Matthew 24:31).

lessons.title: Angels in their place
lessons.body:
Scripture forbids worshipping angels. When John fell at an angel's feet, he was told, "See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant... worship God" (Revelation 22:8-9). Paul warns against "worshipping of angels" (Colossians 2:18).

We do not pray to angels or command them; we pray to God, who sends them as He wills. Christ is far above all angels (Hebrews 1:4-6).

Believers will one day judge angels (1 Corinthians 6:3), and angels long to look into the gospel that saves us (1 Peter 1:12).

terms.def: A created spirit who serves God; the word means messenger.
A chief angel; Michael is called the archangel.
Mighty angels associated with God's throne and guarding the garden.
Angels seen by Isaiah crying 'Holy, holy, holy'.
Angels sent to serve those who will inherit salvation.
Giving angels honour due to God alone, which Scripture forbids.

texts.teaches: Angels are ministering spirits sent to serve the heirs of salvation.
The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear Him.
Michael the archangel did not rail against the devil but said, 'The Lord rebuke thee.'
An angel told John not to worship him but to worship God.
Angels desire to look into the gospel.

summary: Angels are numerous, powerful created spirits.
They worship God, carry His messages and serve believers.
Michael and Gabriel are the only angels named in Scripture.
Angels must never be worshipped or prayed to; Christ is far above them.

questions.q: Which angel is called the archangel?
What did the angel tell John when he fell at his feet?

options: Those who shall be heirs of salvation

modules.title: Satan and the Fall of Angels
modules.intro: Satan is real, but he is a fallen creature, not God's equal. This week we study his origin, names and tactics.

lessons.title: A fallen creature
lessons.body:
God made all things good, so Satan was created good and fell by his own pride. Jesus said the devil "abode not in the truth" (John 8:44). Paul warns that a new convert may fall "into the condemnation of the devil" through pride (1 Timothy 3:6).

Many Christians see Isaiah 14:12-15 (the king of Babylon, "Lucifer, son of the morning") and Ezekiel 28:12-17 (the king of Tyrus, perfect until iniquity was found in him) as also describing Satan's fall behind those proud kings. Others read them only of the human kings.

Other angels followed him: "the angels which kept not their first estate" (Jude 1:6).

lessons.title: Names and works
lessons.body:
His names reveal his character:
- **Satan:** adversary (Job 1:6).
- **Devil:** slanderer, accuser (Revelation 12:9-10).
- **Tempter** (Matthew 4:3).
- **The god of this world**, who blinds unbelievers' minds (2 Corinthians 4:4).
- **Father of lies** and a **murderer** (John 8:44).

His tactics include temptation, deception (he appears "as an angel of light", 2 Corinthians 11:14), accusation, false teaching (1 Timothy 4:1), and persecution (Revelation 2:10). He "walketh about, seeking whom he may devour" (1 Peter 5:8).

lessons.title: On a chain: Satan's limits
lessons.body:
Satan is not God's opposite or equal. He is a creature, limited in power and knowledge, and he can only go as far as God permits. In Job, he could touch Job only within the limits God set (Job 1:12; 2:6).

Jesus told Peter, "Satan hath desired to have you... But I have prayed for thee" (Luke 22:31-32). God never lets believers be tempted beyond what they can bear (1 Corinthians 10:13).

African traditional thought sometimes treats evil powers as nearly as strong as God. Scripture says otherwise: "greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world" (1 John 4:4).

terms.def: The chief fallen angel; the name means adversary.
Satan's title meaning slanderer or accuser.
'Light-bearer', the KJV name in Isaiah 14:12, often applied to Satan before his fall.
Angels who rebelled with Satan; also called demons.
The false idea that good and evil are equal, opposing powers.
Satan's role of accusing believers before God (Revelation 12:10).

texts.teaches: The devil is a murderer and the father of lies.
Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.
The devil seeks whom he may devour; be sober and vigilant.
Satan could only act within limits God set.
Greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world.

summary: Satan was created good and fell through pride, with other angels.
His names show him as adversary, slanderer, tempter and liar.
He works by temptation, deception, accusation and persecution.
He is a limited creature, permitted only what God allows.

questions.q: What does the name Satan mean?
How does 2 Corinthians 11:14 say Satan can appear?
What does the book of Job show about Satan?
options: He can act only within limits God sets

questions.q: Dualism is the false idea that:
options: Good and evil are equal opposing powers

modules.title: Demons and the Victory of Christ
modules.intro: This week we see how Jesus dealt with demons, and how His cross and resurrection defeated the powers of darkness.

lessons.title: Jesus and the demons
lessons.body:
Demons are fallen angels who serve Satan (Matthew 25:41; Revelation 12:9). In the Gospels they oppress people with sickness, madness and torment, though not every illness is demonic; the Gospels distinguish healing from casting out (Mark 1:32-34).

Jesus cast them out by a word, without rituals or objects (Mark 1:25-27). They recognised Him and trembled (Mark 5:7; James 2:19).

He gave His disciples authority over them in His name (Luke 10:17-20), yet told them to rejoice more that their names were written in heaven.

lessons.title: Triumph at the cross
lessons.body:
Christ came "that he might destroy the works of the devil" (1 John 3:8). At the cross He "spoiled principalities and powers... triumphing over them in it" (Colossians 2:15). By His death He destroyed "him that had the power of death, that is, the devil" (Hebrews 2:14-15).

How? Satan's power over us lay in our guilt. By paying for our sins, Christ took away the accuser's case. "There is therefore now no condemnation" (Romans 8:1).

Raised and exalted, Christ is "far above all principality, and power" (Ephesians 1:21), and believers are seated with Him (Ephesians 2:6).

lessons.title: Satan's final end
lessons.body:
Satan's defeat is certain and will be final. Jesus said, "I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven" (Luke 10:18). The everlasting fire is "prepared for the devil and his angels" (Matthew 25:41).

Revelation shows the devil cast into "the lake of fire and brimstone... for ever and ever" (Revelation 20:10). "The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly" (Romans 16:20), fulfilling the first promise of Genesis 3:15.

Believers fight from victory, not for victory. The war is decided; we stand in what Christ has won.

terms.def: A fallen angel serving Satan; also called an unclean or evil spirit.
The casting out of a demon; in Scripture, by the authority of Christ's name.
Ranks of spiritual beings, including evil ones defeated by Christ.
The truth that Christ's death and resurrection conquered Satan and the powers.
The right, given by Christ, to act in His name.
The place of final punishment prepared for the devil and his angels.

texts.teaches: Jesus commanded unclean spirits with authority and they obeyed.
Rejoice more that your names are written in heaven than that spirits submit.
Christ triumphed over principalities and powers at the cross.
Through death Christ destroyed him that had the power of death.
The devil will be cast into the lake of fire for ever.

summary: Demons are fallen angels who oppress people, but not every illness is demonic.
Jesus cast out demons by His word and gave His disciples authority in His name.
At the cross Christ disarmed the powers by removing our guilt.
Satan's final defeat is certain; believers fight from victory.

questions.q: How did Jesus cast out demons?
According to Colossians 2:15, where did Christ triumph over the powers?
What did Jesus tell the seventy to rejoice in most?
For whom was everlasting fire prepared?

modules.title: Standing Firm in Spiritual Warfare
modules.intro: Believers are in a real battle. This week we learn how to stand: the armour of God, resisting the devil, and different views on deliverance.

lessons.title: The whole armour of God
lessons.body:
"Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil" (Ephesians 6:11). Our battle is "not against flesh and blood, but against principalities" (6:12).

The armour is Christ and His gospel applied: the belt of **truth**, the breastplate of **righteousness**, feet shod with the **gospel of peace**, the shield of **faith**, the helmet of **salvation**, the sword of the Spirit, **the word of God**, all with **prayer** (6:14-18).

Notice that it is mostly defensive and ordinary: truth, holiness, faith, Scripture and prayer.

lessons.title: Resist, and give no place
lessons.body:
"Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you" (James 4:7). "Neither give place to the devil" (Ephesians 4:27): unrepented anger, bitterness and secret sin give him a foothold.

Jesus resisted temptation with Scripture (Matthew 4:1-11). Peter tells us to resist "stedfast in the faith" (1 Peter 5:9).

Believers should renounce occult involvement: charms, fortune-tellers, secret societies, ancestral sacrifices. The Ephesian believers burned their magic books (Acts 19:18-19). Christ is enough; we need no other protection.

lessons.title: Can a Christian be demonised?
lessons.body:
Bible-believing Christians answer this differently:

- **No possession of believers:** many Baptists and other evangelicals teach that a true Christian, indwelt by the Holy Spirit and belonging to Christ, cannot be possessed or inhabited by demons (1 John 5:18; 1 Corinthians 6:19). Believers can be tempted, attacked and oppressed from outside, and are delivered through repentance, faith and the Word.
- **Oppression needing deliverance:** many Pentecostal and Holiness churches, including Deeper Life, practise deliverance ministry. Some hold that believers may be oppressed or bound in areas of life (for example through unconfessed sin or past occult involvement) and need prayer for freedom, while affirming that a born-again believer cannot be owned by Satan.

Both agree: Christ's victory is complete, sin must be repented of, and fear has no place.

terms.def: The believer's conflict with the devil, the world and the flesh.
The devil's cunning schemes and strategies.
Truth, righteousness, the gospel, faith, salvation and the Word, with prayer (Ephesians 6).
An opening given to the devil through unrepented sin.
Practices seeking hidden power or knowledge from spirits, forbidden in Scripture.
Freeing a person from demonic oppression through Christ's authority.

texts.teaches: Put on the whole armour of God to stand against the devil's wiles.
Our battle is not against flesh and blood.
Submit to God, resist the devil, and he will flee.
New believers burned their books of magic.
The wicked one does not touch him that is born of God.

summary: Stand in the whole armour of God: truth, righteousness, gospel, faith, salvation, Word and prayer.
Submit to God, resist the devil and give him no foothold.
Renounce all occult practices; Christ is enough.
Christians differ on whether believers can be demonised, but all affirm Christ's complete victory.

questions.q: What is the sword of the Spirit?
What does James 4:7 promise if we resist the devil?
What did the Ephesian believers do with their magic books?
On which point do both views about believers and demons agree?
options: Christ's victory is complete and sin must be repented of
Believers can be owned by Satan

short.q: What are angels, and what do they do?
short.model: Angels are created spirits who worship God, carry His messages and minister to believers.

short.q: Why must Christians not worship or pray to angels?
short.model: Worship belongs to God alone; the angel in Revelation 22 told John to worship God, and Colossians 2 forbids worshipping angels.
Satan was created good and fell through pride; he is a limited creature who can only act as far as God permits.

short.q: How did Christ defeat Satan at the cross?
short.model: By paying for our sins He removed the guilt Satan used to accuse and enslave us, and so triumphed over the powers.

short.q: Name four parts of the armour of God.
short.model: Truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and the sword of the Spirit (the Word of God), with prayer.

short.q: Summarise fairly the two main views on whether a Christian can be demonised.
short.model: One view says a Spirit-indwelt believer cannot be possessed, only attacked from outside; another practises deliverance for believers oppressed in areas of life. Both affirm Christ's complete victory and the need to repent of sin.

lists.q: List four names or titles of Satan.
List three ministries of holy angels.
List five pieces of the armour of God.

assignments.title: Fear or faith?
assignments.prompt: Describe common beliefs or fears about spirits, witchcraft or curses in your community. Using at least five passages from this course, explain how a believer should understand and respond to them in the light of Christ's victory.

assignments.title: Dressed for battle
assignments.prompt: Study Ephesians 6:10-18. Explain each piece of the armour in your own words and give a practical example of how a believer "puts it on" in daily life.

reading: C. Fred Dickason, Angels: Elect and Evil
Clinton E. Arnold, Powers of Darkness
